record.source_closeout_reference: Duration-ladder rung-1 mission LADDER_RUNG1_20260610; envelope, mission state, checkpoints, and interrupt record under docs/Factory/v3/ladder/rung1/; committed with the mission changes per the same_commit convention

mission.objective: Execute duration-ladder rung 1: bring the five state docs into consistency with the nine 2026-06-10 missions, exercising waypoints, checkpoints with all six mission-health signals, authored mission state, and one thread-based Tier 3 interrupt with full lifecycle.

forbidden_scope: no validator, fixture, template, or skill changes
no top-level README or GOVERNANCE_BOUNDARIES.md changes
no new approval or promotion language
allowed_commands: scoped git add, commit, and push after sponsor-approved closeout
fallback_triggers: boundary or approval language weakened by any edit

verification.summary: Per-waypoint verification ran after WP2 and WP3. The WP2 run surfaced V3-A002 on the new mission-state file (missing research-only posture language); classified as accepted true positive, fixed, and re-verified clean. All closeout checks pass.

notes: Docs-only consistency mission with no new dependencies or code paths; conditional ANCHOR_REGISTRY authorization went unused.

Tier 3 interrupt HDI-RUNG1-001 completed the full asked/answered/applied lifecycle: sponsor chose Option A (V3-OP-003 promotion as the next named operational-readiness decision), applied to three state docs with no plan delta.
All six mission-health signals were recorded with citations at each of three checkpoints; budget actuals came from date -u timestamps and tool-call counts, not estimates.
Scope stayed inside the envelope; no fallback trigger fired.
The pause at CP2 for the interrupt was the envelope-planned behavior, not a halt.

friction_notes: Duration honesty: the mission completed in roughly 7 minutes wall clock and ~30 tool calls against a ~90-minute plan. Rung-1 mechanics (waypoints, checkpoints, signals, interrupt lifecycle, mission state) are fully exercised, but the run does not demonstrate behavior at one-hour duration. The sponsor should adjudicate at closeout whether this satisfies rung 1 or whether a genuinely longer mission re-runs the rung; the decision pack's ladder criteria care about mechanics and budget discipline, both of which were met, but elapsed-duration evidence remains thin.
Health-signal cost was 10-15 lines per checkpoint and acceptable; no signal was redundant at this scale.
false_positive_notes: The V3-A002 finding on the mission-state file is classified as an accepted true positive.

Three V3-MR058 findings on this record's first draft are classified as accepted true positives of lint strictness: a directory-prefix authorized_files entry (docs/Factory/v3/ladder/rung1/) does not cover its files under exact matching; the record now lists the three files explicitly. The envelope's directory grant remains the human-readable authority; future records should expand directory grants to explicit paths.
false_negative_notes: No false negatives observed after the final advisory pass.

phase2_design_signals: The envelope's Decision Plan (pre-naming the Tier 3 question and gating one waypoint on it) made the interrupt cheap and the answer immediately applicable; pre-planted decision points should be standard for ladder missions.
A structured in-session question surface produced a clean answer-source record; rung 2 should compare this against the live remote transport for record equivalence.

Harness execution speed compresses wall-clock duration far below human-paced estimates; ladder rung naming should shift from hours to budget-and-waypoint classes, or rung 2-3 missions need genuinely larger scope to produce duration stress.
